Petition filed under Article 226 of the Constitution of India
 seeking a Writ Of Mandamus directing ban use of newspaper and plastic
 bags for wrapping/packing/serving food.
 For Petitioner : Mr.P.R.Balasubramanian
 For Respondent : Mr.S.Namo Narayanan for R1 & R3
 Mr.H.S.Hredai for R2

(Order of the Court was made by S.MANIKUMAR , J.)
Petitioner has sought for a writ of mandamus directing ban on use of newspaper and plastic bags for wrapping/packing/serving food.

2. On the steps taken to prevent usage of newspapers and plastic as packing material, and the circulars issued periodically, Mr.E.Manokaran, http://www.judis.nic.in learned Additional Government Pleader, has filed an affidavit dated 16.4.2019 sworn by the Commissioner of Food Safety, Chennai - 600 006.
Supporting the same, documents have been filed in the typed set of papers.

The affidavit is extracted hereunder:
I, P. Amudha, Wife of Shambhu Kallolikar, aged about 48 years working as Commissioner, Tamil Nadu Food Safety and Drug Administration Department, No.
359, Annasalai, 5th Floor, DMS Office Building, Teynampet, Chennai - 600 006 do hereby solemnly affirm and sincerely state as follows:
1. I am the 4th Respondent herein and I am well acquainted with the facts of the case from the available records and file this Counter.

sentences.text: I deny all the averments made in the above Writ Petition except those that are specifically admitted hereunder.

2. It is submitted that the writ Petitioner had filed a writ of Mandamus to direct the Respondents to Ban use of newspaper and plastic bags for wrapping / Packing /
Serving Food.

2 3.
It is submitted that the Petitioner filed this writ petition to Ban the use of old newspapers and Plastic bags/Sheets to wrap/Pack/Serve Food items in various grounds.

In the writ petition he has stated that unhygienic road side eateries, small and mini sized restaurants and such eateries throughout India are using old newspapers/polythene bags to parcel/wrap/serve the Food items.
This may cause ill health and injury to public health.
Moreover using newspapers which are printed with ink will cause many type of cancer.
Plastic bags used in carrying hot liquid food items like tea, coffee etc, made up of polythene (Polythene) may also cause long and stomach cancer are the allegations / averments of the petitioner.
http://www.judis.nic.in 4.

It is further submitted that in the writ petition the petitioner has stated that Respondents have not taken any steps to ban the usages of newspapers/polythene bags in packing/wrapping serving food items.
It is wholly incorrect and unacceptable one.

5. It is humbly submitted that the Food Safety and standard authority of India sent the Letter to all State Commissioner of Food Safety in file No.1/stds/Newspaper packing/FSSAI - 2016 dated on 06.12.2016 restricting the use of newspaper as food packing material.
In that FSSAI letter it has categorically been stated that what are all the ill effects that will happen to consumer by taking newspaper packed food material.

That FSSAI Letter was circulated to all states Commissioner of Food Safety to initiate a systematic campaign for generating awareness amongst all stakeholders to discourage the use of newspapers for packing, serving and storing of food items.

6. It is further submitted that based upon the Letter of FSSAI, the Commissioner of Food Safety,
Fourth Respondent herein, issued circular in R.No. 9863/2016/SI/FSSA dated on 19.12.2016 and 01.04.2019 to all the Designated Officers to create awareness among the food business operators through the following:-
(a) Press release by district Collectors.
(b) Meeting with food outlets and vendors.
All district Designated Officers, and Food Safety Officers created awareness campaign on restriction to use newspaper for packing food amongst food business operators, consumers, students and Public.
In many places newspapers and food items were seized and destroyed on the spot.

7. It is further submitted that district wise press release, awareness campaign and information education communication http://www.judis.nic.in (IEC) were given to Food Business Operators,
Consumers, Schools and Colleges in this regard by Food Safety Officers.
The details are as follows:-

( a ) All 32 districts in the state have organized awareness meetings regarding ban on using newspaper for packing food items during the period from December 2016 to V.Nandakumar vs The Secretary on 16 April, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/57158548/
3 March 2019.
In Schools/Colleges overall 567 awareness meetings were conducted by Food Safety Department.

To food business operators overall 788 awareness meetings were conducted and about 80484 Food Business Operators were inspected during that period for restraining use of news paper for packing food items.
For public and other stakeholders, 437 awareness meetings were conducted.

Moreover with regard to restriction of use of newspaper for packing of food items and polythene cover packing, awareness notices, pamphlets were issued and overall 3968.5 Kg of newspaper which was kept for food packing were seized and destroyed in all 32 districts.

(b) Press release:
Press releases have been issued through concerned District Collectors in all Districts to sensitize the Food Business Operators and the Public.
(c) Whatsapp Complaint:
During the month of May 2017, The Food Safety Department of Tamil Nadu Launched a Whatsapp Number "9444042322 for complaint redressal on Food Safety issues in Tamil Nadu.

sentences.text: Awareness is being created among Food Business Operators and the consumers in all Districts.

The public are encouraged to lodge complaint on any Food Business Operator related to Food in the aspects of Adulteration, Hygiene and other contravention of the Food Safety and Standards Act,
etc.
The Food Business Operators are promoted to display the Whatsapp Number at their premises.

Once the Complaints are received, http://www.judis.nic.in they will be communicated to the concerned area Food Safety Officer by the Head Quarters of Food Safety Department at Chennai for immediate action within 24 hours.

8. It is submitted that on the International Environmental day on 05.06.2018, the Honble Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu announced on the floor of the Assembly a ban to use certain plastic items,
including non-woven carry bags, from 01.01.2019 to gift a plastic - free state to future generations.
The ban on manufacture, sale, storage and usage of items such as plastic paper, Sheets, cups, water sachets, straws and carry bags came into effect from January 1, 2019.
However, polythene sachets used for packing milk, curd, oil and medical equipment would be exempted from the ban.
When such disposable plastic items remain on the soil, it impedes water flow to water bodies, resulting in stagnation; It also affects the flow of sewage.
Further, it prevents percolation of rain water into the soil, thus affecting the availability of ground water.
In this connection, in all 32 districts in TamilNadu awareness meetings over ban on One time and throw away plastics were conducted from 01.04.2018 to 31.12.2019.

For Hotels, Street Vendors,
Other Food Business Operators overall 478 awareness meetings were conducted by Food Safety Department.
For educational Institutions 302 evens and Self Help Groups & Other Consumer Forums 189 awareness meetings were conducted.

Various Programmes were organized and conducted with regard to ban of newspaper and plastic items for packing and serving food items through Information Education Communication (IEC) activities in Schools, Colleges and food business operators (FBO).

the Food Safety Officers issued pamphlets and awareness notices to Public.

Food business operators were addressed in implementing the government order banning certain plastic items and also create awareness on ill effects of plastic on human health by using News papers for wrapping & packaging of food items.

11. It is further submitted that one time usable Plastic ban came in to force on 01.01.2019 throughout Tamil Nadu the Food Safety Officers, Designated Officers inspected various hotels, shop,
market, restaurants, stall and many places and found banned plastic products seized and destroyed them.
In many cases concern authorities seized the banned products and destroyed as per rules.
After implementation of plastic ban now many hotels are using permitted aluminum foil as packing material along with Banana Leaf and other eco friendly options.

Dated, the 06th December, 2016 Subject: Restricting the use of newspaper as food packaging material 1. Use of newspapers for wrapping, packing and serving food is a common practice in India.
However, this is a food safety hazard.
Wrapping food in newspapers is in unhealthy practice and the consumption of such food is injurious to health, even if the food has been cooked hygienically.
Indians are being slowly poisoned due to newspaper being widely used as food packaging material by small hotels, vendors and also in homes in lieu of absorbent paper.

V.Nandakumar vs The Secretary on 16 April, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/57158548/
5
2. Foods contaminated by newspaper ink raise serious health concerns since the ink contains multiple bioactive materials with known negative health effects.
Printing inks may also contain harmful colors, pigments, binders, additives, and preservatives.

Besides chemical contaminants,
presence of pathogenic microorganisms in used newspapers also pose potential risk to human health.

3. Newspapers and even paper / cardboard boxes made of recycled paper may be contaminated with metallic contaminants, mineral oils and harmful chemicals like phthalates which can cause digestive problems and also lead to severe toxicity.

Older people, teenagers, children and people with compromised vital organs and immune systems are at a greater risk of acquiring cancer-related health complications, if they are exposed to food packed in such material.
4. Newspapers should not be used to wrap, cover, and severe food or to absorb excess oil from fried food.

There is an urgent need to discourage the use of newspapers as food packaging material by creating awareness among businesses, especially unorganized food business operators and consumers on its harmful effects.
Suitable steps needs to be taken to restrict and control the use of newspapers for packing of food material.

5. Commissioners of Food Safety of all States/UTs are requested to initiate a systematic campaign for generating awareness amongst all stakeholders to discourage the use of newspapers for packing,
serving and storing of food items.
(Kumar Anil) Advisor (Standards) To Commissioners of Food Safety of all States/UTs http://www.judis.nic.in

11. It is further submitted that one time usable Plastic ban came in to force on 01.01.2019 throughout Tamil Nadu the Food Safety Officers, Designated Officers inspected various hotels, shop,
market, restaurants, stall and many places and found banned plastic products seized and destroyed them.
In continuance of the above activities, all Designated Officers are instructed to carry out the follwing:
1. Create awareness regarding the avoiding the use of old newspapers and Plastic bags/sheets to wrap/pack/serve food items among the FBOs and Community through Pamphlets, Awareness notices and press release through District Collectors.
2. Inspection of FBOs to ensure the avoiding the use of old newspapers and Banned Plastics to Wrap/pack/serve food items.
The action taken report should be sent this office at once.
For Commissioner of Food Safety To All Designated Officers.
